## Changes
- **Right-click the path bar to change its size.** Right-click the path bar along the top of an editor pane and choose Small, Medium, Large or Extra Large, the same as Path bar size in Foolscap › Settings… › Editor.
## Fixes
- **Very long pastes are asked about.** Pasting or dropping text longer than any book (more than about 2 MB, or 350,000 words) now asks first, because text that long can slow Foolscap down, and every snapshot and backup keeps a copy of it. More than 20 MB at once isn't pasted; paste it in parts instead. Titles and an entry's other names are now kept to one line of up to 500 characters. - **Long scenes save faster.** Saving a scene takes a fraction of the time it did, most of all for a very long one: a whole book pasted into one scene saves around 20 times faster, or two to three times faster with italics or other formatting in it. - **Emoji next to formatting are kept.** Where italics, a highlight, a comment or other formatting started or ended in the middle of an emoji, saving replaced the emoji with “�”. The emoji is now kept whole.

## Changes
- **The path bar can be larger or smaller.** Choose Small, Medium, Large or Extra Large for Path bar size in Foolscap › Settings… › Editor. It sets the size of the path along the top of each editor pane (Manuscript › Chapter › Scene) and of its Back and Forward buttons. Medium is how it looked before. - **Commented words are tinted instead of underlined.** The orange dotted underline was hard to see, so commented words now have a pale orange tint, and the comment you’re on is a deeper orange. Words you’ve highlighted keep their highlight color and get the dotted underline instead. With Differentiate without color turned on in System Settings › Accessibility › Display, commented words have both the tint and the underline.
## Fixes
- **Compare shows pictures and tables that changed.** Comparing a snapshot with the current text showed a picture or table you'd taken out as if it were still there. A removed picture or table is now faded and crossed out in red, and an added one is outlined in green. A picture replaced by another or resized, and a table whose contents changed, now show as the old one removed and the new one added. - **Snapshots show their text again.** Choosing a snapshot in the Snapshots inspector showed a blank page with the snapshot bar at the bottom, because the bar took the whole height of the editor. The snapshot's text now fills the editor, with the bar underneath. Items in the Trash had the same problem: the Put Back bar took the whole editor, so a trashed scene's text couldn't be read. That's fixed too.

## Changes
- **Foolscap › License…, ready for when Foolscap goes on sale.** A new License tab in Foolscap › Settings… activates a license key on a Mac, and deactivates it to move it to another. One license works on up to five Macs. Test versions, numbered below 1.0, don't need a license, so nothing changes for them yet. From 1.0, Foolscap works fully for 30 days on each Mac, then opens projects read-only until a license key is entered. Please don't buy a license yet: the Buy Foolscap… button goes to the real store, and test versions don't need one.
## Fixes
- **VoiceOver in the Revision Report.** Each place listed under a word, phrase or scene now says which scene it's in, as holding the pointer over it does. A scene in Changes reads "120 words added, 45 cut", and the report's title is a heading, so VoiceOver's headings rotor finds it.

## Getting started
- **A Welcome window the first time Foolscap opens.** It asks whether Apple Intelligence's Writing Tools and predictive text are offered while you write (Foolscap picks neither for you), and lets you choose a theme, where new projects are saved, and spelling and grammar checking. Each choice is in Foolscap › Settings… too. It shows once on each Mac, and not at all if you've used Foolscap before, here or on another device, so updating won't show it. - **A short tour of the project window.** After the Welcome, the first project you open points out the binder, the format bar, the status bar, the inspector, the switcher between the editor, timeline and pages, and Project › Tools. Choose Help › Show Tour Again to see it whenever you like. - **The Foolscap Tutorial.** Choose Help › Foolscap Tutorial for a project that teaches Foolscap by doing: a chapter each on writing, organizing, notes and goals, the Story Bible and timeline, revising, exporting, and non-fiction and papers, with a short story to try things on. It's a fresh copy each time, and isn't saved unless you choose to keep it.

## Themes
- **One Theme setting replaces Page color and Corkboard.** Choose it in Foolscap › Settings… › Editor. **Ink** is a white page with a deep blue corkboard, **Paper** a cream page with a kraft brown corkboard, and **Blotter**, which is new, a pale green page with a deep green corkboard. Each has a dark form, which follows Appearance. - **Your colors may change when you update.** White becomes Ink, and Paper stays Paper, with its new kraft brown board. A page and a board can no longer be mixed freely, and the Quiet corkboard is gone, so a board set to Quiet now takes the theme's color. - **A theme colors more of the window.** With Paper and Blotter, the toolbar, the side panels, what's chosen in them, the timeline and Book Shape all follow. Ink leaves those in your Mac's own colors, as before. Printing, exports and the pages in Page Preview still stay black text on white.
## Point of view
- **Say how each scene is told.** The Point of View menu now offers **1st Person**, **3rd Person** and **3rd Person Limited**. 1st Person and 3rd Person Limited can name a character, in a second pop-up menu beside the first in the inspector. 3rd Person is an all-knowing narrator, and names no one. - **Scenes that already had a point of view are now 3rd Person Limited.** Change any told in the first person to 1st Person, and they keep their character. Scrivener imports come in the same way. - **It shows wherever point of view does.** A card shows the character, or how the scene is told if it names no one, and holding the pointer over it shows both. Book Shape gives scenes that name no one a color and a line of their own, and Find in Project can list the scenes told each way. - **Emptying the Trash** now leaves a scene told the same way when its character is deleted, naming no one.
## Fixes
- **On Paper, the toolbar and the New Scene bar no longer turn white over the corkboard.** - **Adverbs, Passive Voice, Filter Verbs and Dialogue Tags no longer stay empty for want of language data.** On a Mac without the data for the project's language, they could find nothing, with no explanation. Foolscap now asks macOS to download it when the revision aids first read the project, and reads the text again once it arrives, so they may stay empty until then. Only the data is downloaded: your text stays on your Mac, and nothing is downloaded with **Recognize parts of speech** off. - **Book Shape fills its pane again.** It could open squashed at the top of the editor, with the tallest bar drawn over the legend and the rest of the pane empty. - **A scene on its own no longer gets its name as a heading.** In Page Preview and when printing, This Scene put the scene's binder name over its text as a chapter heading in every layout, though the book never prints it. A scene named after its first words seemed to start with its first line twice. Now the first scene of a chapter opens under the chapter's heading, as it does in the book, and any other starts at the top of the page. Several scenes chosen together and This Snapshot do the same. - **A reading copy's first chapter starts its own page.** With front matter, Chapter One ran on under the last front matter page, in PDFs, Word and RTF, and in Page Preview. It now opens on a new page like every other chapter. - **A reading copy no longer starts with a blank page** when its first front matter page is one you wrote, rather than a title page. - **The paperback preview no longer titles scenes with the book's name.** Previewing a scene or several scenes as a paperback put the project's title over them as a chapter heading. - **A chapter printed alone looks as it does in the book.** A chapter in a part has its heading at the size it has in the whole manuscript, and numbered headings keep their numbers.

## Changes
- **Timeline dates can be BC.** For a book set in the ancient world, choose BC when you set the date of Day 1. Dates read as history books write them, such as March 15, 44 BC, with no year 0 and no weekday, and they go back as far as 4713 BC. A book set AD also gets dates for days that reach back past the year 1. A project with a BC date needs this version: an older one drops the date of Day 1. - **Give a scene its day by its date.** With Dates on, click the date under the day in the When row, or Set Date… for a scene with no day yet, and choose a date. The scene moves to that day, so you don't have to count the days yourself. - **Choosing the date of Day 1 has changed.** It now has fields for the month, day, year and era, with the calendar for dates AD, and nothing changes until you click Set. - **Long gaps on the timeline read in years.** A gap of a year or more between scenes now says "About 16 years later" rather than "5766 days later". - **The format bar steps aside on the corkboard.** It's hidden wherever there's no text to format, so a chapter's cards get its room. - **The format bar has an Insert menu.** A `+` takes the place of the Scene Break and Page Break buttons, with everything in the menu bar's Insert menu, footnotes and comments among them. The bar has more room, and keeps its buttons in a narrower window. - **The corkboard says how long the chapter is.** The status bar now gives the chapter's words beside the manuscript's. - **Progress says "1 word cut".** A day or a stretch that cut more than it added no longer reads "-1 word in all · -1 a day". - **Empty notes say what they're for.** The inspector's Notes show a prompt until you type in them. - **The New Project window is larger,** so every template is in view with its whole name. - **Scene names take two lines in the binder.** A long name wraps rather than being cut after a few words, and the sidebar opens wider. A window still at the old narrow width widens once. - **A scene's status takes the place of its page icon.** Every scene had the same icon; now the row shows where the scene stands. A scene with no status keeps its icon, and chapters and notes keep their marks at the end of the row. - **The corkboard's cards look like index cards.** A paper color, a serif title on up to two lines, a red rule, and ruled lines for the words, with the status and word count along the foot. Dark mode's cards now stand out from the board. - **Cards share the board's width,** with no empty strip down the side, and a card whose title is just its opening words doesn't say them twice. - **The corkboard is the blue of Foolscap's ink.** For a quieter board that follows the page, choose Quiet for Corkboard in Settings › Editor. - **With Paper, the whole window follows the page.** The toolbar and format bar turn cream with it, and the sidebar and inspector warm up to match.
## Fixes
- **A paperback with footnotes numbered again on each page no longer crashes.** With that setting, one footnote and more than one chapter, choosing Paperback in the page preview, opening the Paperback tab of Export or printing a paperback took the app down. - **Contents and lists have the right page numbers with footnotes numbered on each page.** A heading or caption near the end of a page could be listed on the page next to it, more often the more notes came before it. - **Edits to the title, copyright and other made pages are kept after Revert.** After Revert or Restore from Backup, those pages showed the old project, and what you changed on them was lost on saving. - **The inspector stays filled in after Revert.** After Revert or Restore from Backup it stayed empty until you chose another item. - **A damaged .bib file no longer crashes the app.** A file cut off inside a quoted value now imports what it can. - **Typing is smoother in long papers and theses.** With cross-references or numbered captions, renumbering waits until you pause, rather than going on every moment as you type. A second pane with the same scene, a live search, or a References, Notes or Contents page keeps up with less work too. - **Emptying a full Trash is much quicker,** and so is undoing it. - **Typing in Settings › Writer is smoother.** Open texts are redrawn, and your details sent to iCloud, when you pause. - **Make Full-Page Image can't change the wrong image any more.** Clicking an image in a snapshot offered it, and it acted on the scene as it is now. A snapshot's images no longer offer changes. - **Typing at the start of a paragraph takes that paragraph's style.** With the cursor before a bold first word, what you type now comes out bold, rather than taking the style of the end of the paragraph before. - **A footnote pasted with paragraph breaks stays on one line.** Some text copied from other apps could keep a break inside a note. - **What you're typing in a field is kept when you save, close or quit.** A synopsis, comment, title, Day or other field still being typed in was lost if you saved, closed the window or quit before leaving it. Exporting, printing and backing up now include it too, and your cursor stays where it was. - **Changes from your other devices no longer hold up the window.** A project with lots of images is now read in the background when another device's changes arrive, so typing carries on while they come in. - **A comment on a paper's run-in heading is kept in Word.** Word dropped a comment that ended in a heading set at the start of its paragraph. - **A thesis with only a title and a date keeps them on one page.** In a PDF the date went onto a page of its own, and in Word it stopped short of the foot of the page. - **Setting a date applies to what you opened it on.** Choosing another scene, or reverting, now closes the date pop-overs on the timeline and in the When row.

## Changes
- **Foolscap now comes as a DMG too.** New downloads can use a disk image as well as the zip. Updates inside the app work as before.
## Fixes
- **VoiceOver reads the Progress tab's counts as one thing.** A count and its "words" were two stops, and now they're one: "53 words".

## Changes
- **A No AI Training page for your book.** Click + beside the Front Matter's heading and choose No AI Training to add a page saying the book isn't to be used to train generative AI. It goes after the Copyright page, starts with standard wording that you can change, and is printed under its title in every export that has the front matter. No project has it unless you add it.
## Fixes
- **Foolscap starts with the New Project window again.** With no project to reopen, it was showing the standard Open window instead. Open Existing… and Open Recent are in the New Project window if a project is what you're after. - **Add Comment and Add Bookmark are dimmed when they have nothing to mark.** With the insertion point away from any word, Add Comment still appeared in the Insert menu and the text's Control-click menu, and only made an alert sound. Add Bookmark did the same on an empty line. Both still work with nothing selected when there's a word or a paragraph to go on.

## Changes
- **Your name and contact details follow you.** If you're signed in to iCloud, what's in Settings › Writer is now the same on every Mac you use: change it on one and the others follow. The newest change wins, and your other settings stay with each Mac. If you already have different details on two Macs, the first to open this version sets them for both, so check Settings › Writer afterwards. - **Footnotes show as numbers, and a click opens them.** A note's words no longer appear among the text, so View › Show Footnotes and Hide Footnotes are gone. Click a note's number to read or change it, or hold the pointer over it to read it. Find still looks in footnotes: when it finds words in one, the note opens with them chosen. A snapshot still shows each note's words, so that you can see what's changed in them. Your notes are saved and exported as they always were.
## Help
- **Sending a paperback to the printer.** The Paperback PDF page has a new section, Sending it to the printer, for when the PDF is made: get the ISBN first and export again so the copyright page shows it, give KDP or IngramSpark the same trim size, paper and bleed as Paperback Settings, make the cover to the size the Export sheet gives, then check every page in KDP's Print Previewer and order a proof copy. Choose Help › Foolscap Help and look under Paperback PDF.
## Fixes
- **Writing Tools no longer damages footnotes.** Rewriting text with a footnote in it could change the footnote's words and turn it into ordinary text, showing OBJ boxes. Now footnotes leave the text you've chosen while Writing Tools works, so a sentence is rewritten as a whole, and each goes back after the word it followed, or at the end of the sentence if that word has gone. Images, tables, citations, cross-references, breaks and words with a comment or bookmark are left as they are, and if a change would still damage one, Foolscap takes it back and says so. - **The inspector's chosen tab shows its icon again.** On macOS 27, the tab chosen at the top of the inspector was a plain blue block with no icon, because the icon was drawn in the same blue as the tab's background. It now shows in white, so you can see which tab is open. Nothing changes on macOS 26. - **Restoring from a backup now always saves what it restored.** Restoring just after making changes could show the backup's words in the window while the project on disk kept the words being replaced, so they came back the next time it opened. It now saves the backup's words every time. - **Saving on two Macs while they can’t reach each other now works as it should.** macOS could ask which version to keep instead of Foolscap putting them together, and choosing one took the other out of the project. A scene changed on both could also lose one version with no snapshot. Foolscap now puts them together itself: the newer text stays, the older is kept as a snapshot, and an alert tells you which is which. "Not synced" also no longer flashes up while this happens. - **Foolscap now says when a project didn't open.** The Open window can occasionally close without passing the project on, and then nothing happened. Now an alert tells you, so you can try again.

## A steadier iCloud status
A small fix for projects kept in iCloud Drive.
- **No more brief "Not synced".** iCloud sometimes reports a problem for a moment as a project opens, then clears it, and the status bar showed "Not synced" for that moment. Now it says so only when the problem lasts a few seconds, as it already did for "Uploading to iCloud…".

## Getting ready for iCloud
This version starts the work on keeping a project in iCloud Drive and writing in it on more than one Mac. Projects are now saved a little differently, ready for it.
- **Keep projects in iCloud Drive.** Settings has a new General tab: set New projects to iCloud Drive, and the save panel opens in iCloud Drive's Foolscap folder. Move a project you have already with File › Move To…. While iCloud is uploading or downloading a project, or can't sync it, the status bar says so, and a project that isn't on this Mac yet downloads in a window before it opens. See Help › Keeping a project in iCloud.
- **Each Mac remembers its own place.** A project opens where you left off on the Mac you're using: the same scene, place in the text, split editor and open folders. On a Mac it's new to, it opens where you last left it on any Mac. - **A project open on two Macs keeps up.** If your Macs share a project through iCloud Drive or Dropbox, changes saved on one now come into the other as they arrive, without reopening it, and the status bar says which Mac they came from. When both Macs changed the same paragraph of a scene, your text stays and the other Mac's is kept as a snapshot, and Foolscap tells you. See Help › Getting started › Working on more than one Mac. - **Earlier versions can't open projects saved by this one.** Once you save a project in this version, an earlier Foolscap says it was made by a newer version. Update Foolscap on each of your Macs before opening your projects there.

## Test versions expire
From this version on, each test version of Foolscap expires about three months after it's made, so old copies don't stay in use. Updating before then keeps everything as it is.
- **Two weeks before**, the status bar at the bottom of a project's window says when, as in "Expires 28 January". Click it for more, or to check for updates. - **Once expired**, Foolscap says so when it opens, and the status bar says **Read-only**. Your projects still open, and you can read, search, print and export them, and copy from them. Changes aren't saved and new projects can't be made. Nothing in your projects is changed. - **Foolscap › Check for Updates…** gets the current version, which saves as usual. The alert and the status bar both have a button for it. - **Help**: Test versions, under Updates on the Settings page.
